# Whole-segment extrusion and a sharp triangle roof capacity

This is an actual planar geometric lemma for the proper-A, zero-B
critical-circuit regime. It does not resolve the general OC statement.
All areas below are ordinary planar area. No numerical evidence is used.

## 1. Coordinates and the entire swept segment

Use x,y with t=-x-y and the canonical triangle

    T={x<=1, y<=1, -x-y<=1},       |T|=9/2.

Let A,B,K be planar convex bodies, B subset T and (A+B)/2 subset K.
Assume the t projection of A is [l,h] with l<-1 and h>2. Write

    b=|B|, H=h+1>3, q=|K intersect {t>=0}|.

Choose actual points of A attaining l,h. Their segment is in A.
In the area-preserving coordinates (t,s), s=x-c t, this segment
has constant s=s_A for a real c. The map (x,y)->(t,s) has
determinant1. For each s in the projection of B, write its actual
vertical section as [L(s),U(s)]. Because B subset T,

    -2<=L(s)<=U(s)<=1.

The corresponding section of segment+B, at s_A+s, is exactly
[l+L(s),h+U(s)]. Its lower endpoint is negative and upper endpoint
positive. Thus its part in t>=0 has length h+U(s). Consequently

    4q >= R_c(B,h):=integral (h+U(s)) ds.                 (1)

The midpoint homothety accounts for the factor4. This contains the
WHOLE swept segment plus B, not a sum of unrelated inclusions.
Sections of zero length and projection endpoints are harmless null
sets. All halfspaces are closed; their boundary lines have area zero.

Pointwise, for every section,

    h+U - H(U-L)/3
      =[(h-2)(1-U)+H(L+2)]/3 >=0.

Integrating first yields the simple bound

    4q>=Hb/3,             b<=12q/H.                    (2)

## 2. Sharp capacity for an arbitrary direction of the segment

In fact, for every B subset T as above and every c,

    R_c(B,h) >= H[3-sqrt(9-2b)].                       (3)

Here 0<b<=9/2, so the square root is well-defined. We prove this
without a regularity assumption on B or its boundary.

Let L_T,U_T be the endpoints of the t sections of T in the same
coordinates, and let v_T=U_T-L_T. For almost every nonempty B
section let v_B=U-L. Define

    r_c(s)=(h+U_T(s))/v_T(s)

on the interior of T's transverse projection, where v_T>0. Then

    h+U=v_B+(h+L)
          >= v_B[1+(h+L_T)/v_T]=r_c v_B.              (4)

Indeed L>=L_T, 0<v_B<=v_T, and h+L_T>0. Put v_B=0
outside B's projection. Thus R_c>=integral r_c v_B, with
0<=v_B<=v_T and integral v_B=b.

We compare the distribution of r_c under the area measure

    dmu_c(s)=v_T(s) ds,            mu_c(total)=9/2.

For -1<=c<=0 the top of T is U_T=1. The chord length increases
linearly from0 to3, then decreases linearly to0. The two branch
changes of variable from s to v_T have absolute derivatives
1+c and -c, whose sum is1. This includes c=0,-1, when one branch
has zero length. Hence the distribution is

    dmu_0(v)=v dv, 0<v<3,       r_0(v)=H/v.

In particular its lower distribution function is

    F_0(lambda)=0                         if lambda<H/3,
                 9/2-H^2/(2lambda^2)      if lambda>=H/3.       (5)

For c>0 put m=1+c. The three vertices in increasing s order are
(-2,1), (1,-2), (1,1), with respective t values1,1,-2.
The two branches now have 0<v<3/m. On the first branch,

    ds=m dv,       U_T=1,       r_c=H/v.

On the second branch,

    |ds|=cm dv,    U_T=-2+m v,  r_c=m+(H-3)/v.

Both ratios have minimum Hm/3. For lambda>=Hm/3 their lower
distribution function is therefore exactly

    F_c(lambda)=9/2-mH^2/(2lambda^2)
                    -cm(H-3)^2/[2(lambda-m)^2].       (6)

The denominator is positive because H>3 and lambda>=Hm/3>m.
For smaller lambda the function is zero. It follows at once that

    F_c(lambda)<=F_0(lambda)  for every lambda>=0.      (7)

The case c<-1 follows by interchanging x,y: t stays fixed, the
new slope is -1-c>0, and the transverse coordinate changes sign.
Thus (7) holds for every c, with equality of distributions on
the entire interval -1<=c<=0.

For completeness the distribution comparison gives a direct integral
inequality, without assuming a minimizing B exists. For every lambda>=0,

    integral r_c v_B
      >=lambda b-integral (lambda-r_c)_+ dmu_c
       =lambda b-integral_0^lambda F_c(u)du
      >=lambda b-integral_0^lambda F_0(u)du.           (8)

The first inequality uses 0<=v_B<=v_T separately where r_c is
below and above lambda; the identity is Tonelli for a nonnegative
integrand. If b<9/2, put v_0=sqrt(9-2b)>0 and choose
lambda=H/v_0. In the baseline distribution, the region v>=v_0
has area integral_(v_0)^3 v dv=b. The final expression in (8)
therefore equals its baseline cost

    integral_(v_0)^3 (H/v)v dv=H(3-v_0).

This proves (3) for b<9/2. At b=9/2 take lambda to infinity
in (8), or let v_0 decrease to0 in the same explicit formulas;
the lower bound tends to3H. No varying bodies or selected points
are involved in this scalar limit.

The constant in (3) is sharp for this standalone roof problem.
Take any -1<=c<=0 and intersect T with the transverse strip where
v_T(s)>=v_0. This is a convex body for 0<=v_0<3. It has area
(9-v_0^2)/2, its upper roof is1, and its transverse width is
3-v_0. Thus its roof cost is exactly H(3-v_0). This is a claim
of sharpness for (3), not simultaneous equality in criticality,
positive area of A, or the mixed-integer conjecture.

Combining (1) and (3) proves the stronger actual cap bound

    4q >= H[3-sqrt(9-2b)].                            (9)

## 3. Consequence for the current bad critical-circuit regime

In the notation of the all-level endpoint note, the ordinary profiles
and a hypothetical bad nonheavy-B configuration give

    b >= (9/4)q+(5/2-r)w,   w>0, 0<r<1.

Thus q<4b/9. Equation(9) implies the strict height restriction

    H < (16/9)[3+sqrt(9-2b)]/2
       = (8/9)[3+sqrt(9-2b)] <=16/3.                (10)

The rationalization uses b/[3-sqrt(9-2b)]
=[3+sqrt(9-2b)]/2. All of the stronger positive w terms can be
retained in (9); they were discarded only in deriving (10).

These inequalities may be combined with the whole-A lower-tail
height bound, the shifted three-cap cover tail charge, and the
affine-selector restriction. No claim that this combination closes
the full critical-circuit regime, or OC, is made here.

## 4. An additive reserve from the actual upper part of A

The swept-segment estimate retains a further positive area term:

    4q >= R_c(B,h)+tau,
    tau=|A intersect {t>=2}|.                         (11)

In particular the sharp roof capacity strengthens to

    4q >= H[3-sqrt(9-2b)]+tau.                       (12)

Here is a complete proof that does not add overlapping subsets as if
they were disjoint. After the determinant-one shear of Section1,
translate A and its actual segment S by -s_A in the transverse
direction, leave B fixed, and translate K by -s_A/2. These tangent
translations preserve all areas, the tested cut, and (A+B)/2 subset K.
The translated S is {0} times [l,h]. Write the sections of A as

    [a_-(t),a_+(t)],       a_-(t)<=0<=a_+(t), l<=t<=h.

Put D=S+B and C=A+B. Both have the same longitudinal projection,
and D subset C. On every interior longitudinal level v, their
sections are intervals. Thus the gain in their section widths is
the sum of two individually nonnegative boundary gains,

    (right_C(v)-right_D(v))+(left_D(v)-left_C(v)).

Let (s_+,t_+) be a rightmost point of B, so s_+=max_B s and
-2<=t_+<=1. For t in [-t_+,h], put v=t+t_+. Then v>=0,
t>=-1>l, and the point (s_+,t_+) is admissible in the section of
D at level v, by adding (0,t) in S. Therefore right_D(v)=s_+.
Adding (a_+(t),t) in A shows

    right_C(t+t_+)-right_D(t+t_+)>=a_+(t).

The interval [-t_+,h] is nonempty and contains [2,h]. Integrate
over these v levels and use nonnegativity of the right-boundary
gain at all other nonnegative levels. The resulting lower bound
for the integrated right gain is integral_(-t_+)^h a_+(t)dt.

Choose likewise a leftmost point (s_-,t_-) of B. The corresponding
integrated left gain is at least integral_(-t_-)^h -a_-(t)dt.
Adding the two gains is legitimate even when their v intervals
overlap: they are the two distinct summands of the section-width
difference. We have proved the more precise estimate

    |C intersect {t>=0}|-|D intersect {t>=0}|
      >= integral_(-t_+)^h a_+(t)dt
                       +integral_(-t_-)^h -a_-(t)dt
      >= integral_2^h [a_+(t)-a_-(t)]dt=tau.          (13)

Section1 identifies |D intersect {t>=0}|=R_c(B,h), so (11)
follows from C/2 subset K. Endpoint sections and boundary lines
are null and cause no extra terms. If a transverse supporting face
of B has several points, choosing its highest t improves the exact
reserve in (13); no uniqueness is assumed.

When both transverse extreme points can be chosen at t=1, the
stronger reserve in (13) is precisely

    integral_(-1)^h [a_+(t)-a_-(t)]dt
      =|A intersect {t>=-1}|=w.

This includes the strip extremizers of the roof problem when
-1<=c<=0, and recovers the original full-facet additive w term.
For general B only the tau bound is asserted uniformly.

In the actual bad-circuit regime, the already proved shifted
three-cap cover gives tau>=delta_*=a-v-u/4. Thus (12) may use
that explicit common-body mass in place of tau.

## 5. A larger explicitly excluded near-full endpoint regime

The same bad regime gives H>=2sqrt(3), by delta/w>=1/4 and
the upper-tail homothety. Combining this with the strict inequality
(10) yields

    sqrt(9-2b)>9sqrt(3)/4-3>0,
    b<(216sqrt(3)-243)/32,
    b/|T|<(24sqrt(3)-27)/16.                         (14)

Therefore endpoint area fraction at least (24sqrt(3)-27)/16 is
already excluded in this particular proper-A/zero-B critical
regime. This conclusion does not require B to contain any specified
homothetic inner triangle. It uses the exact whole-segment geometry;
the strictly positive additive reserve in (12) can only strengthen
it. No extension to arbitrary critical menus is implicit.
